misconceptions_note: All 40 original catch-all check:'wrong' misconceptions deleted and replaced with 47 expect-matched ones (0 to 3 per problem). Expects derived by committing each error: e.g. silver[3] included_anomaly 511 ÷ 9 = 56.8, divided_by_9 391 ÷ 9 = 43.4; gold[1] divided_by_15 9.5 ÷ 15 = 0.63, forgot_to_remove 18 ÷ 14 = 1.29; gold[3] mean_over_range (14 ÷ 4) × 100 = 350; bronze[2] range 5.2 − 0.3 = 4.9. For multiple choice, expect is the distractor index.
opener_concept: Picking 10 students to speak for a school of 200 that is 160 Year 10 and 40 Year 11. Box 1 is the common-sense even split (5 each), box 2 finds Year 10's real share (0.8), box 3 shares the 10 places fairly (8). The reveal names it as stratified sampling. A small inline SVG bar shows the 160/40 split so the figure claimed is actually on screen.
notes: No image or chart stimulus exists in this lesson (all data sits in the display text), so every problem was fresh-solved rather than trusted; nothing needed flagging. Added: tier_guides (bronze/silver/gold), guided.opener, guided.teach for all three tiers (5 boxes each, all off-bank), problem_bank.{bronze,silver,gold}_description, a hint on all 20 problems (12 had none), and guided_steps on 19 of 20 problems. gold[4] carries guided_skip_reason: it is the genuinely evaluative 'why is random sampling impractical' item the spec cites, with no numeric route to the option. Because there is no map or graph, each walk's first box locates the student in the data instead (count the readings, read the interval, find the scale maximum) before any arithmetic. Classification multiple-choice problems are worked with numeric boxes plus 1/0 yes-no diagnostic boxes, with the final say-step naming the option. Every walk ends with a check box that rebuilds the total, the sample size or the range it started from. method_card slimmed from 5 steps / ~300 words to 4 steps / 129 words; related_videos, topic_links and worked_examples preserved (worked_examples touched only to remove one em dash).
